To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The chance of two different users choosing the same free hand gesture for a given action is low.

(1) users tend to choose different gestures to perform the same task; (2) users tend to agree more with the gestures suggested by the interface; (3) users tend to disagree more on gestures with multiple degrees of freedom; (4) users tend to be more consistent on gestures with less degrees of freedom; and (5) users tend to produce gestures with a higher degree of freedom for tasks that require more precision.

(1) users have different gesture preferences for the same task, (2) offering a set of candidate gestures improves the agreement score, and (3) the gesture disagreement is related to the task's difficulty and the number of gestures users can choose.
